As applied to flood events, the recurrence interval is the average interval of time within which a given flood will be equaled or exceeded once. Frequencies of floods can be stated in terms of their probabilities of occurrence (reciprocals of their recurrence intervals). For example, a flood with a 25-year recurrence interval would have a 4 percent chance of being equaled or exceeded in any given year.
Profiles of the water surface, based primarily on elevations of marks left by the floods of October 1954, July 1957, September 1961 and April 1965 are shown in Exhibit "25"to"28"for the creeks and tributaries involved in the Lincoln Highway improvement. Where floodmarks could not be obtained, the profiles were constructed on the basis of flood crests determined from photographs and from reports of local residents, and of elevations of streambeds and lower flood stages. River miles used for the profiles correspond to those marked along the rivers on the flood map.
A total of five box culverts will be constructed in conjunction with this project. The standard practices for building this type of structure will be employed, including the partial damming of the streams involved or the diversion of the stream around the work area during the construction period. This involvement of the waterways is not considered to have a significant detrimental impact because the construction will take place during periods of low volume flow in the streams. The upgrading in size of the existing inadequate culverts to handle the flow from a 50 year storm is deemed essential to help alleviate upstream flooding conditions.
Proposed structures for this roadway improvement are designed to carry a 50 year storm and the closed drainage system is based on a ten-year storm. Therefore, the major structures according to present design standards should adequately carry all waters to the downstream side of the roadway. The existing structures are incapable of carrying the flow resulting from the design year storm and therefore, cause flooding in the area upstream from the crossing.
